stories.title: Dev-bridge 'page not connected' error hardcodes localhost:5173 regardless of actual port
engine doctor QA + Proposed-story inbox lines disappear when no sprint is active
stories.summary:
engine/tools/doctor/project-doctor.ts:1943-1948 — `formatBacklog` early-returns from the no-active-sprint branch (`if (report.active === undefined)`). The Recent commits, Follow-ups, QA inbox, and Proposed-story inbox sections (all at the bottom of the function, lines 1973-2026) never get to render in that branch. Surfaced post-S099 merge: S099 is archived, no sprint is active locally, and even though 8 GDP-* files sit in backlog/proposed-stories/, the doctor output skips straight from `Backlog: 95 sprint file(s), 95 archived. No sprint is currently active.` to the Recommendations section. The same affects S093 QA-DOCTOR-INBOX: with no active sprint, QA tickets in the inbox are invisible from the doctor. This is exactly the WORST time for those signals to disappear — between sprints is when the dev terminal should be planning the next one, and the doctor is the canonical 'what needs my attention' view. The S099 AGF-DOCTOR-PROPOSED-STORIES unit test (tests/unit/doctor-proposed-inbox.test.ts:23) only covers the active-sprint path (`status: 'active'`), which is why this slipped through.

QA repro
--------
severity: major · type: bug · filed: 2026-05-20T18:02:46.036Z · PR #114 · under sprint S099

Steps:
  1. From a fresh `origin/main` checkout (HEAD 6d4dc1f, post-S099 merge), confirm no sprint JSON has `"status": "active"`: `grep -l '"status": "active"' backlog/sprints/*.sprint.json` returns nothing.
  2. Confirm there's content in the proposed-story inbox: `ls backlog/proposed-stories/*.story-proposal.json | wc -l` — currently 8 files (GDP-2026-05-20-003 through -010).
  3. Run `npm run engine:doctor -- examples/kaboom-crew` (or `engine:check`).
  4. Scroll to the `Backlog:` section. Observe the entire output of that section is just one line: `Backlog: 95 sprint file(s), 95 archived. No sprint is currently active.` Then the doctor jumps straight to the Recommendations block.
  5. Notice the missing lines that the S099 AGF-DOCTOR-PROPOSED-STORIES acceptance promises: `Proposed-story inbox: 8 pending (...)` and the per-proposal listing. Also missing: the S093 QA-DOCTOR-INBOX line, plus Recent commits and Follow-ups (S087 + S086 stories).
Expected: When the doctor runs against a project with no active sprint, the Backlog section still surfaces QA inbox + Proposed-story inbox + Recent commits + Follow-ups beneath the `No sprint is currently active.` summary. Concretely: with 8 GDP-* files in `backlog/proposed-stories/`, the line `  Proposed-story inbox: 8 pending (...)` should appear regardless of whether a sprint is active. Same for QA inbox per S093.
Actual:   `formatBacklog` returns early at line 1948 in the no-active-sprint branch, so every line below — including the QA inbox (S093), Proposed-story inbox (S099), Recent commits (S087), and Follow-ups (S086) sections — is skipped. The dev terminal sees a one-line `Backlog:` summary at the exact moment those signals matter most (between-sprint planning).

Logs:
engine/tools/doctor/project-doctor.ts:1943-1948
  if (report.active === undefined) {
    lines.push(`Backlog: ${report.sprintFiles} sprint file(s), ${report.archivedCount} archived. No sprint is currently active.`);
    if (report.multipleActive.length > 1) {
      lines.push(`  AGF_BACKLOG_MULTIPLE_ACTIVE: ${report.multipleActive.join(", ")}`);
    }
    return lines.join("\n");  // ← Early return skips QA inbox, Proposed inbox, Recent commits, Follow-ups.
  }

Fix outline: hoist the active-sprint-specific blocks (stories/blocked/multiple-active) into the `if (report.active !== undefined)` branch, then let the function flow into the QA inbox + Proposed-story inbox + Recent commits + Follow-ups sections unconditionally (those gates are already `if (report.foo !== undefined)`-style and tolerant of empty input).

Test gap: tests/unit/doctor-proposed-inbox.test.ts:23 only covers `status: 'active'`. Add a sibling test asserting the proposed-inbox line still renders when every sprint is archived.

Live evidence (just ran `npm run engine:doctor -- examples/kaboom-crew` on post-S099 main):
  Backlog: 95 sprint file(s), 95 archived. No sprint is currently active.

  Recommendations:
    ...

No `QA inbox`, no `Proposed-story inbox`, no `Recent commits`, no `Follow-ups` — every signal that depends on the bottom half of formatBacklog is gone.

stories.title: Doctor 'Procedural mesh registry' line silently lost when bootstrap aliases the registry to a local var
stories.summary:
engine/tools/doctor/project-doctor.ts:964 — `summarizeProceduralMeshes` discovers registered keys via the regex `/proceduralMeshRegistry\(\)\.register\(\s*["']([^"']+)["']/g`. This locks the scan to the literal call form `runtime.renderer.proceduralMeshRegistry().register("...", ...)`. S101's procbomber-bench bootstrap used exactly that form and the AGF-PROCMESH-DOCTOR-LINE acceptance — 'Procedural mesh registry: 1 declared key(s) [procbomber], 1 scene entity reference(s)' — was correct at S101 merge. S102 PROCBOMBER-MESH-TREE-V0 refactored the bootstrap to alias the registry once + register 6 part keys, the common readable pattern: `const procRegistry = runtime.renderer.proceduralMeshRegistry(); procRegistry.register("procbomber-torso", ...); ...` (5 more lines). The aliased form is correct runtime code but the regex never sees `proceduralMeshRegistry()` immediately adjacent to `.register(...)`, so `declaredKeys` collapses to `[]` and `formatProceduralMeshes` suppresses the whole section. Net effect: the doctor's procedural-mesh observability is silently gone the moment a project registers more than one key (the natural moment a developer aliases the helper). Scene-side static count (`sceneUsageCount`) is also 0 for procbomber-bench because the 19-entity bomber tree is spawned at runtime via `bomber-tree-spawner.ts`, not declared in `scenes/start.scene.json` — that's by design, but it means the section relies entirely on `declaredKeys` and the regex must be permissive enough to catch the aliased pattern. Not a regression in the runtime registry (proc meshes render fine — confirmed via `runtime.renderer.proceduralMeshRegistry()` returning the live keys when introspected from `window.__agf`), only in the doctor's static scan.

QA repro
--------
severity: minor · type: bug · filed: 2026-05-21T11:05:13.567Z · PR #118 · under sprint S102

Steps:
  1. From a fresh origin/main checkout (HEAD 4cde337 or later), run `npm run engine:doctor -- examples/procbomber-bench`.
  2. Scroll the output looking for a 'Procedural mesh registry:' line. There is none.
  3. Confirm the bootstrap genuinely registers 6 keys: `grep -n 'register("procbomber' examples/procbomber-bench/bootstrap.ts` — 6 hits (torso/head/upperArm/forearm/upperLeg/lowerLeg).
  4. Confirm the static scan is the failure point: `node -e "const fs=require('node:fs'); const body=fs.readFileSync('examples/procbomber-bench/bootstrap.ts','utf8'); const re=/proceduralMeshRegistry\(\)\.register\(\s*[\"']([^\"']+)[\"']/g; let m,keys=[]; while((m=re.exec(body))) keys.push(m[1]); console.log('Regex caught:', keys);"` — prints `Regex caught: []`.
  5. Confirm runtime is fine — boot `?project=procbomber-bench` in the browser, then `window.__agf.runtime.renderer.proceduralMeshRegistry().keys()` lists all 6 keys (registry is populated at runtime, only the offline scan is blind).
Expected: When a project registers procedural mesh keys — whether via the inline `proceduralMeshRegistry().register(...)` form OR via the natural alias `const procRegistry = ...proceduralMeshRegistry(); procRegistry.register(...)` form — engine doctor reports `Procedural mesh registry: 6 declared key(s) [procbomber-torso, procbomber-head, procbomber-upperArm, procbomber-forearm, procbomber-upperLeg, procbomber-lowerLeg], 0 scene entity reference(s)` (or whatever counts apply). The per-key sub-list still appears for any keys that scenes reference but the project never registers (the existing ⚠ flag).
Actual:   Doctor output skips the 'Procedural mesh registry:' section entirely. The format function's suppression gate (`if (report.declaredKeys.length === 0 && report.sceneUsageCount === 0)`) fires because the static-scan regex doesn't catch the aliased `procRegistry.register(...)` form. Devs (and the dogfood doctor section that was supposed to surface this) get no signal that a project has procedural meshes at all.

Logs:
engine/tools/doctor/project-doctor.ts:957-965
  // S101 AGF-PROCMESH-DOCTOR-LINE: best-effort static scan.
  // - declaredKeys: walk every .ts file under the project for the pattern
  //   `proceduralMeshRegistry().register("<key>"` (single OR double quotes).
  // ...
  const declaredSet = new Set<string>();
  const registerRegex = /proceduralMeshRegistry\(\)\.register\(\s*["']([^"']+)["']/g;

Fix outlines (any of these would close the gap; pick one + add coverage):
  - Two-pass scan: first sweep for `(?:const|let|var)\s+(\w+)\s*=\s*[^;]*\bproceduralMeshRegistry\(\)` to learn the alias names, then sweep for `\b(alias)\.register\(\s*["']([^"']+)["']` per alias. Catches the common pattern + survives renames within a file.
  - Single-pass relaxed regex: `\.register\(\s*["']([^"']+)["']` anchored to files that contain the substring `proceduralMeshRegistry`. Cheap, risk of false positives if a file mentions the registry helper AND has unrelated `.register(...)` calls; OK for a best-effort doctor signal.
  - AST parse via the TS compiler API. Cleanest but heavier; the rest of the doctor's static analysis is regex-based, so this would be the odd-one-out.

Live evidence (post-S102 main):
  $ npm run engine:doctor -- examples/procbomber-bench 2>&1 | grep -i 'procedural mesh'
  (no output)

Referenced acceptance lines:
  S101 PROCBOMBER-BENCH-PROJECT: "engine:doctor shows 'Procedural mesh registry: 1 declared key(s) [procbomber], 1 scene entity reference(s)'." — passed at S101 (inline form); broke at S102 refactor without anyone noticing.
  S101 AGF-PROCMESH-DOCTOR-LINE: "section is suppressed entirely otherwise" — currently suppressed even when 6 keys ARE declared, because the scan never sees them.

Test gap: tests/unit/doctor-procedural-meshes.test.ts (if it exists — needs a check) probably only exercises the inline form. Add a fixture that uses the alias pattern.

Source ticket: QA-2026-05-21-001
